author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Rhode Island’s seasonal fluorescent-orange requirement takes effect Saturday, September 12, as archery hunting gets underway on public lands. The Department of Environmental Management says the rule applies through February 28 to people entering state management areas and undeveloped state parks during hunting season.

Visitors must wear at least 200 square inches of solid fluorescent orange, an amount that can generally be met with an orange hat or vest. The requirement is intended to make hikers, dog walkers, birders and other outdoor users more visible to hunters sharing the same properties.

Archery hunters are exempt from the orange requirement while participating in archery deer season, according to DEM. Other rules can vary by activity and season, so hunters and recreational visitors should review current regulations before entering public land.

The agency’s reminder is especially relevant during the early fall overlap between popular hiking weather and expanding hunting activity. Bright clothing, awareness of posted notices and keeping pets under close control can reduce avoidable conflicts. DEM also advises visitors to know the boundaries and allowed uses of the property they plan to enter.
dek: Visitors to state management areas and undeveloped state parks must wear at least 200 square inches of fluorescent orange from September 12 through February 28.
headline: Rhode Island blaze-orange rule begins as archery season opens
